page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Work out the bracket B − C
steps.margin_note: First mark. The bracket is the whole of this mark. Write B − C = {2} on its own line.
lines: B − C is the set of members of B that are not in C.
3 and 4 are in C, but 2 is not, so B − C = {2}.

recall.must_convey: That B − C keeps the members of B not in C, giving {2}.
accept: B minus C keeps what B has and C does not, that is two
remove three and four from B, only two is left
the bracket comes to the set two
B lo unna, C lo leni elements matrame teesukovali
B minus C equals the set containing two

steps.why: Set difference is not associative, so the bracket must be done first. Reading the question left to right as (A − B) − C would give {1}, a different set.
common_mistakes: Writing B − C = {5, 6}, which is C − B.
Writing B − C = ∅ after assuming every member of B lies in C.
Working out A − B first and ignoring the bracket.
steps.memory_tip: B − C starts from B and crosses out anything C also holds, so the answer is always part of B.

steps.label: Take that set away from A
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show the line A − {2} before the answer, so both moves are on the page.

accept: take two out of A and one and three are left
A minus the set two gives one three
the answer is the set one three
A nunchi two teesestey one and three migulutayi
only members of A can appear so the answer is one and three

steps.why: Only members of A can survive a difference that starts with A, and 2 is the single member of A that also lies in B − C.
common_mistakes: Doing (A − B) − C instead, which gives {1} and is a different set.
Including 4, 5 or 6 in the answer; nothing outside A can appear in A − (B − C).
Removing 3 as well, because 3 is in B.
steps.memory_tip: Sets are subtracted from the inside bracket outwards, the same order as in ordinary arithmetic.
